title: Two of the same laser instead of beam splitter?

posts.topic_title: Two of the same laser instead of beam splitter?
posts.author: Nnnn
posts.post_subject: Two of the same laser instead of beam splitter?
posts.content_md:
Happy holidays!

I got a surprise christmas present from my wonderful sister: the exact same integraf holography kit that I started out with 

It's great to have more plates and developing formula, but I'm a bit curious about the lasers. I understand that for two beam setups it's important to have two beams as similar to each other as possible, so splitting one beam is optimal. But if there's two of the exact same model (diode) laser, should I be able to reproduce a multi beam setup without any mirrors/splitters?

Cheers!

posts.topic_title: Two of the same laser instead of beam splitter?
posts.author: HoloM
posts.post_subject: Two of the same laser instead of beam splitter?
posts.content_md: No, it will not work, as the two beams are not coherent and will never be. You have to use one beam from the same source.

posts.content_md: Good to know, thank you! That's about the answer I expected, but I'm grateful to have it confirmed without wasting any plates.
